claim: Keyed option "The wine was blended from wine grown in two or more member states" and explanation "Once wine or fruit has crossed a border and been blended, no single country can be claimed"
because: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/33, Art. 45(1) allows 'European Union wine' in two cases. Point (b) covers wine blended from wines of several Member States. Point (c) covers wine made in one Member State from grapes harvested in another, with no blending needed. So the line does not tell the buyer that the wine is a blend. Grapes that crossed a border and were vinified unblended carry it too, and both the keyed option and the explanation leave out that second case.
fix: Option 3: "The wine was blended from wines of two or more member states, or made in one member state from grapes harvested in another". Explanation opening: "Once wine is blended across member states, or grapes from one member state are made into wine in another, no single country can be claimed, so the union as a whole becomes the provenance."
